extracted.intended_audience: corporate communicators, public relations professionals, crisis managers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and guidance for corporate crisis communication responses (what to say, when to act, and how to preserve trust) based on the Samsung Galaxy Note 7 case. Focuses on public statements, recalls/replacements, accuracy, and stakeholder updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and frequent communication
rubrics_metrics.description: "Communicating swiftly and often with key audiences is the cornerstone of any crisis response, and Samsung nailed this."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make immediate public statements and keep key audiences updated often to show the company is taking the situation seriously; example: Samsung immediately made public statements and issued a global recall within weeks. Anti-pattern: silence or infrequent updates that allow rumors to grow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of information
rubrics_metrics.description: "However, it’s critical that the information a company shares about the situation is accurate. This is where Samsung went wrong."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify facts before making public claims; inaccurate statements lead to retractions and loss of trust. Example failures: initially saying Hong Kong phones were not at risk (then retracting) and attributing explosions to the battery on incomplete evidence. Scoring note: accuracy outweighs speed when incorrect facts will cause greater harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid acting on incomplete evidence / avoid premature conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: "The company acted too quickly and many of its initial statements had to be retracted."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not draw or announce definitive causes until investigations are sufficiently conclusive. Anti-patterns include confidently stating a root cause based on incomplete data (Samsung blamed the battery prematurely), which can spark further crises if later disproved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit uncertainty and commit to ongoing updates
rubrics_metrics.description: "Samsung could have salvaged a lot of trust, and dollars, if the company had stated that they did not know the cause of the explosions but would keep the public updated as it worked to uncover the root of the problem."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When cause is unknown, publicly acknowledge uncertainty and promise regular updates on investigation progress. This builds credibility and preserves trust better than false certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughly validate fixes before large-scale rollout
rubrics_metrics.description: Samsung produced 2.5 million replacement phones after its initial battery explanation, but "the replacement phones started exploding, too."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any corrective action (repairs, replacements, fixes) must be rigorously tested and validated before mass deployment; rushing a remedy can create a second, worse crisis. Example anti-pattern: shipping unproven replacement units that repeat the failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take decisive, visible safety actions (recalls, discontinuation) when warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: "It immediately made public statements about the news and issued a global recall of the phones within weeks... Samsung finally conceded... and was forced to discontinue the Note 7 altogether."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete actions like recalls or product discontinuation demonstrate seriousness and can be necessary to protect consumers and restore confidence. Guidance: pair decisive action with clear communication explaining rationale and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect stakeholder trust and measure reputational/financial impact
rubrics_metrics.description: "By providing inaccurate information and acting too quickly, Samsung lost the trust of its customers and investors... Its stock took a nosedive... plunging 7 percent in one day."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize communications that preserve customer and investor trust; track reputational and financial indicators (stock movement, customer sentiment) as outcomes of the PR response. Mistakes in messaging can magnify financial losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance speed with accuracy — primary PR takeaway
rubrics_metrics.description: "From a PR perspective, the biggest takeaway is to share information early and often, but make sure the information you're sharing is accurate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The central standard for crisis PR is balancing prompt, frequent communication with rigorous fact-checking. Practical approach: rapid acknowledgement of the situation + clear statement of what is known/unknown + scheduled updates after investigation.
